I don't hate it as much as most, but didn't love it as much as you did. I do regularly listen to the soundtrack. Cliff Martinez is a wizard.

On the other hand, Only God Forgives absolutely left me breathless. Probably my favorite Refn film.

I saw it recently for the first time. I was captivated the whole time but not sure if I actually liked it while watching it. Then after I let it stir in my mind for the rest of the day, the more I appreciated it.

Visually and aurally it was amazing, it felt like a very ambitious music video. The scene with the track "Are We Having a Party?" was just such a unique pairing, then of course the runway scene was beautiful.

Also I still laugh in my head when I remember the "Your name's Bean?" line.
Cliff Martinez!

> The exploitative nature of the fashion industry was being held up for us to see, but it was far from preachy. Jesse was empowered by her own beauty, not victimised by it.

Kinda disagree with this. Reminder, Jesse was 16 years old (if I remember correctly). She's a child, enchanted with the American dream, but unaware of the seriousness of the whole business. I don't think she had any idea what she got herself into. Hollywood is a rotten world, where you're completely on your own, despite everyone acting like the nicest person on earth. Your landlord tries to rape you, and even your closest friend wants to literally cannibalize you.

But I agree with everything else you say. Such a captivating movie! It's one of my favorites and def my favorite Refn movie. You've probably seen it already, but another gem from Refn is Drive, I've heard some people call The Neon Demon "the female version of Drive" so you kinda know what to expect. Another must-watch from Refn is Only God Forgives.

Refn is my favorite filmmaker alive. I’ve only seen the Neon Demon once but I think about it all the time. I know his movies aren’t for everyone, but they certainly are for me lol. Always glad to see someone else loves this film.
The quote I always think about is “I ate her.”

I found it fascinating how Jesse was so ambiguous tbh. There was certainly elements that made you feel she was out of her depth, a naive ingenue. And then there were those striking moments of power and poise where she seems to have a mysterious inner strength, where she didn't act like you'd expect an innocent 16 year old to act. Her expression and reaction at the photo shoot, especially afterwards where she acted like it had been a fulfilling experience for her, not a truanatic one. When she saw the wildcat and her look seemed to share something with it. When there was that weird scene with the triplicating of her, as she kissed her two images within the neon triangles. When she stood in the diving board and announced she was dangerous. There was definitely something more going on under the surface expectations of "unprotected 16 year old lost in LA". I can't put my finger on it though.

I love that movie

One of the best movie experiences I had this year

Great points! It's been a while since I've seen the movie but I guess I have to agree with you. I was thinking only about that photography scene but the things you mentioned brought up some memories.

Also, now that we're talking about it. Pleasure (2021) has a similar story, just a bit more explicit than the Neon Demon (porn star vs fashion model).

My opinion is actually the opposite. Though I liked the visuals and soundtrack of Only God Forgives I really didn't like how it executed its story. I dont dislike either movie but I was a lot more affected by Neon Demon.

As someone who's been always a bit fascinated by Refn ever since seeing Drive in cinema, The Neon Demon felt a bit like Refn's answer to the critique of Only God Forgives - A more steamlined experience, with more digestible themes for people to get behind. Still, with his strengths on full display, it managed to etch out a few key scenes in my mind through engrossing visuals.

Not long ago Refn made a mini-series "Too Old To Die Young", and it's him absolutely not holding back from the very first minute.
For me the line that made to movie was: "What about you? Are you Food or are you Sex?"

I just watched following your suggestion - it was something I'd been planning to do for so long anyway. 

I thought it was fine, but it didn't really grip me in the way that other Refn films do. I think for me the problem is that the film inhabits a strange space, neither realistic nor fantastic, and I think it doesn't do either tendency complete justice. 

For the first part, despite heavily stylised photography, there is no obvious sign that it's going to veer into much more fantastical territory later. This part, of getting to know Jesse, is generally low-energy and unconvincing, the dialogue particularly being quite weak. I just didn't buy at any time that Jesse was a simple country girl from Georgia, nor that her friend Dean was a good-hearted kid who just wants to help. More authenticity at this point would have helped the turn later to much more wild and fantastic material all the more effective. But a lot of it was dull. 

The last third was much better, but still lacked a little extra to make it truly transgressive. Despite the sensational scenes that came at the end, it was actually a very predictable turn into violence and quite conventional in its dynamic. 

Since you ask for comment on the ending I'll just say this: it's a common magical belief that if you eat someone, you will gain their power. That's what it means, pretty basic really.

I was completely baffled by Only God Forgives, and just felt kind of ill after Neon Demon, but have an odd feeling I will revisit both at some point.

Too old to die young was a mix of both. One of the most pretentious things I’ve ever watched but the good moments were just so good.
